newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber quiet in post-holiday blues.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber quiet in post-holiday blues.

text.p: Trading in the Singapore rubber market was quiet by midday on Thursday as players trickled back after a national holiday yesterday, dealers said.
A holiday in Indonesia weighed on sentiment in the local exchange while marginally easier prices in Tokyo failed to provide any clear direction to the market, they said.
"There's nothing up basically. It was fairly quiet and I did not see any offers being requested. Nothing was done this morning," a dealer said.
"Like most morning sessions recently, it was very quiet. We're hoping for better conditions in the afternoon," one said.
The only feature in the market was news that European and Asian buyers were engaged in buying about 6,500 tonnes of SMR20 rubber.
"That's the only action so far, especially since Indonesia is out," a trader said.

At 0445 GMT, July RSS3 rubber was indicated at 113.25 U.S. cents a kg from 114.00 cents last Tuesday. July RSS1 was indicated at 162.50 Singapore cents (US$1.13) a kg from 163.00 cents. July TSR20 was indicated at 154.25-156.25 Singapore cents (US$1.07-$1.09) a kg from 156.25 cents.
